Harold Weisberg wrote to Julia Shea on June 11, 1980 about a records fight with the FBI's Dallas field office. Weisberg had filed Privacy Act requests for files the office held. He reports that the office complied only in part and withheld records he believed were his to see.

The letter is a progress report from a long campaign of requests and appeals. Weisberg spent years forcing assassination records out of the Bureau, office by office. Dallas held central files on the Kennedy case, so its refusals mattered. His account to Shea preserves the state of that fight in mid-1980.

The paper reports the erosion found after the long test. Such turbines were candidates for making electricity in space from a nuclear heat source.

Filmmaker Bart Sibrel joins the Joe Rogan Experience for episode 2141 to make his case that the moon landings were faked. Sibrel has spent decades on the claim, confronting astronauts and building films around the footage he calls staged. Rogan gives the skeptic a full hearing.

Sibrel lays out his best points, from flag movement to radiation belts, and tells of his run-ins with the Apollo crew. Rogan tests the arguments and asks what proof would change Sibrel's mind. The episode preserves the moon-hoax case in its most committed form, useful for anyone who wants to hear it whole before judging it.
